title: Dua when waking up
preview: Thank Allah for returning your soul and giving you a new day. Recite as soon as you open your eyes.
arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
content:
# Dua when waking up

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ

**Transliteration:** Alhamdu lillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhi an-nushur.

**Meaning:** All praise is for Allah who gave us life after having taken it from us, and to Him is the resurrection.

---

**When to recite:** As soon as you wake up, before getting out of bed.

**Why it matters:** Every morning is a gift. This dua turns the first moment of your day into gratitude and remembrance of the One who sustains your life and will raise you on the Day of Judgment.

*Reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6312*

title: Dua when leaving the house
preview: Seek Allah’s protection and guidance whenever you step out. Recite before you leave home.
content:
# Dua when leaving the house

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

بِسْمِ اللهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللهِ وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ

**Transliteration:** Bismillahi tawakkaltu 'ala Allahi wa la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

**Meaning:** In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah; there is no power and no strength except with Allah.

---

**When to recite:** Before stepping out of your home, with your right foot first.

**Why it matters:** You are placing your day in Allah’s care. Whatever happens outside – work, travel, errands – you have asked for His protection and acknowledged that real strength comes only from Him.

*Reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5095, Tirmidhi 3426*
arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللهِ وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ

title: Dua for entering the mosque
preview: Ask Allah to open for you the doors of His mercy when you enter the masjid.
arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
content:
# Dua for entering the mosque

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

بِسْمِ اللهِ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللهِ، اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ

**Transliteration:** Bismillahi wassalatu wassalamu 'ala rasulillah. Allahumma aftah li abwaba rahmatik.

**Meaning:** In the name of Allah, and blessings and peace upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

---

**When to recite:** When you enter the mosque, stepping in with your right foot first.

**Why it matters:** The mosque is a place of mercy and remembrance. This dua prepares your heart and asks Allah to make your prayer, your focus, and your time there a means of receiving His mercy.

*Reference: Sunan Ibn Majah 771, Sahih Muslim 713*

title: Dua for leaving the mosque
preview: Ask Allah for His bounty as you leave the masjid, so your step into the world is still connected to Him.
content:
# Dua for leaving the mosque

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ

**Transliteration:** Allahumma inni as'aluka min fadlik.

**Meaning:** O Allah, I ask You from Your bounty.

---

**When to recite:** When you leave the mosque, stepping out with your left foot first.

**Why it matters:** You are not leaving Allah when you leave the masjid. This short dua keeps you asking Him for His favour – in provision, in guidance, in barakah – as you go back to your daily life.

*Reference: Sahih Muslim 713*

title: Dua before eating
preview: Begin every meal in the name of Allah so your food is blessed and your eating is an act of worship.
content:
# Dua before eating

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

بِسْمِ اللهِ

*(If you forget at the start: بِسْمِ اللهِ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَآخِرِهِ.)*

**Transliteration:** Bismillah. (Or: Bismillahi fi awwalihi wa akhirihi – In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.)

**Meaning:** In the name of Allah.

---

**When to recite:** Before you take the first bite. If you forget, say *Bismillahi fi awwalihi wa akhirihi* when you remember.

**Why it matters:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that when you mention Allah’s name before eating, Satan cannot share in that meal. A simple “Bismillah” turns your food into a blessed provision and keeps the act in remembrance of the One who provided it.

*Reference: Sahih Muslim 2022, Abu Dawud 3767*

title: Dua after eating
preview: Thank Allah after your meal. The Prophet (ﷺ) said whoever says this is forgiven.
arabic: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
content:
# Dua after eating

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَذَا وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ

**Transliteration:** Alhamdu lillahi alladhi at'amani hadha wa razaqanihi min ghayri hawlin minni wa la quwwah.

**Meaning:** Praise is to Allah who fed me this and provided it for me without any might or power from myself.

---

**When to recite:** When you finish your meal.

**Why it matters:** You acknowledge that the food and the ability to eat it both come from Allah. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that whoever says this after eating, his past sins are forgiven. Gratitude completes the blessing.

*Reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 4023, Tirmidhi 3458*

title: Dua when entering the home
preview: Greet your home and ask Allah for the best entry and exit whenever you come back.
content:
# Dua when entering the home

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

بِسْمِ اللهِ وَلَجْنَا وَبِسْمِ اللهِ خَرَجْنَا وَعَلَى رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا

**Transliteration:** Bismillahi walajna wa bismillahi kharajna wa 'ala rabbina tawakkaltu.

**Meaning:** In the name of Allah we enter, in the name of Allah we leave, and upon our Lord we rely.

---

**When to recite:** When you enter your home (and you can also say the full greeting: *Bismillahi walajna...* and *Assalamu 'alaykum* for those inside).

**Why it matters:** Your home is a place of rest and family. Starting your entry with Allah’s name and trust in Him invites barakah and keeps the house under His care. It pairs with the “leaving home” dua – you begin and end your outings with Allah.

*Reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5096*
arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ وَلَجْنَا وَبِسْمِ اللهِ خَرَجْنَا وَعَلَى رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا

title: Dua when entering the bathroom
preview: Seek refuge in Allah from evil when entering the toilet. A sunnah of the Prophet (ﷺ).
content:
# Dua when entering the bathroom

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

بِسْمِ اللهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبْثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ

**Transliteration:** Bismillah. Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min al-khubthi wa al-khaba'ith.

**Meaning:** In the name of Allah. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from male and female evil (evil spirits and harmful things).

---

**When to recite:** Before entering the bathroom or toilet, preferably with the left foot first.

**Why it matters:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught this to seek Allah’s protection in a private place where we are vulnerable. It is a brief but powerful habit that keeps you in remembrance and under His refuge throughout the day.

*Reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 142, 6321*
arabic: بِسْمِ اللهِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبْثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ

title: Dua when leaving the bathroom
preview: Ask Allah for forgiveness and purification when you leave the toilet. Completes the sunnah of the bathroom.
content:
# Dua when leaving the bathroom

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

غُفْرَانَكَ

**Transliteration:** Ghufranak.

**Meaning:** I ask You (Allah) for forgiveness.

---

**When to recite:** When you leave the bathroom or toilet, stepping out with the right foot first.

**Why it matters:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) would say *Ghufranak* upon leaving the toilet. It is a short, easy sunnah that turns a daily routine into a moment of seeking Allah’s forgiveness and purification. Together with the “entering” dua, it bookends the act with remembrance and repentance.

*Reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 30, Ibn Majah 300*

title: Dua before sleeping
preview: End your day in Allah’s name. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught this before sleep for protection and remembrance.
content:
# Dua before sleeping

**Arabic** *(display in large font):*

بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَمُوتُ وَأَحْيَا

**Transliteration:** Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya.

**Meaning:** In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.

---

**When to recite:** When you lie down to sleep, preferably on your right side after reciting Ayatul Kursi and the last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah if you can.

**Why it matters:** Sleep is a small death; waking is a small resurrection. This dua reminds you that both are in Allah’s hands. You fall asleep in His name and under His care, so the night becomes a time of trust and remembrance, not fear.

*Reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 6312*
